tool.name: qpcrpredict report
tool.description: HTML report from one or more qpcrpredict prediction tables
tool.command: @INSTALL_QPCRPREDICT@ #for $i, $t in enumerate($tables) ln -s '$t' 'table_${i}.tsv' && #end for #for $r in $runs ln -s '$r' '$r.element_identifier' && #end for python -m qpcrpredict.cli report #for $i, $t in enumerate($tables) 'table_${i}.tsv' #end for #for $r in $runs --run '$r.element_identifier' #end for #if str($title).strip() != '' --title '$title' #end if #if str($assay_source.source) == 'history' --assay '$assay_source.assay' #end if --out '$html'

param.name: tables
param.label: Prediction tables
param.help: One or more outputs of the qpcrpredict tool. They are merged into one report; each keeps its run.

param.name: runs
param.label: Run files (optional)
param.help: The .eds or RDML files the tables were computed from. When given, the report shows the amplification curves of every sample. A run file is matched to its table by the file name it had when the prediction was made, so upload the same files.

param.name: source
param.label: Assay
param.help: The assay configuration used to read the run files for the curves.
param.option: Built-in assay: AML molecular MRD (reference ABL1)

param.name: title
param.label: Report title
param.help: For example the batch or run name.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Writes one self-contained HTML page from one or more prediction tables of the ``qpcrpredict`` tool: an overview of the calls, one section per run with the call, probability, Ct, reference copies, ratio and reasons of every analysis, and, when the run files are given, the amplification curves of the target and reference wells of every sample. Filters, search, sorting, font size and a light or dark theme are built into the page; it needs no network access.
**Inputs**
* *Prediction tables* - one or more outputs of ``qpcrpredict``. * *Run files* (optional) - the ``.eds`` or RDML files the tables were computed from, for the curves. * *Assay* - the configuration used to read the run files. * *Report title* - shown in the header.
**Output**
An HTML file. Open it in the browser from the history.
